keyFindings.description: The deadline fatal names no observation. The old loop's t.Fatalf("sweep reported %+v", obs) printed the Kind and Detail of the wrong verdict, which is how LEGION-370 was diagnosed (Kind:uncertain Detail:... no current target, from CI). The new loop discards every pre-final observation and the deadline path's t.Fatal carries nothing, so a classifier stuck on Uncertain, one stuck on Alive, and a silent sweep all print one identical line; CI runs go test without -v (.github/workflows/envoy-and-contracts.yaml:672), so that line is the whole evidence a triager gets. Every other fatal in this file names its observation (:620, :1278, :1300). Fix: keep `var last runtime.Observation`, assign it in the observations arm, and fail with t.Fatalf("the sweep never reported the killed pane gone; last = %+v", last). The leading substring stays, so the recorded NC-1/NC-3 proof strings stay valid.

Comment precision, same push: (a) `(machine.go)` is not a file of this package; cite internal/supervise/machine.go:806, and cite observe.go:58-60 for 'reports either once' (the package's other cross-file references carry path and lines, e.g. verify.go:24, spawn.go:161); (b) Alive is 'a probe that read /proc before the process died', not 'a probe whose list-panes ran before the kill' (verifyPane reads /proc after the listing, verify.go:141-174, so the latter is also the straddle the comment describes at :1308-1309); (c) 'or a client killed by its timeout' is not a state the kill leaves, and with CommandTimeout 10 s (:499) equal to the loop's deadline it cannot be waited through in this rig; drop the clause.
Fast-follow: '(the supervisor's one death)' in the doc comment restates :1310; the loop comment is where the fact and its citation belong.
